data.title: 25 years of agricultural transformation: From Gujarat’s growth journey to farmer prosperity
data.description:
Over the past 25 years, Indian agriculture has undergone a foundational shift largely driven by investments in irrigation, rural infrastructure, farm technology and direct grower support. Under Narendra Modi’s leadership, first in Gujarat and later at the Centre, strengthening rural livelihoods has remained central to India’s development trajectory. This productive capacity is reflected in the nation’s food grain output, which reached an estimated record of 357.73 million tonne in 2024-25.

The next chapter of this journey requires a broader benchmark of success. While national food security remains fundamental, agricultural progress must also translate into sustainable farm incomes, healthier soils, disciplined water use and greater economic resilience for the smallholder.

Gujarat’s experience: Development through ground-level action

Gujarat’s agrarian turnaround offers valuable lessons on how water governance, rural infrastructure and community engagement can strengthen agricultural productivity in arid regions. Measures such as water conservation, combining the Sardar Sarovar canal work with decentralised check dams, farm ponds and micro-irrigation, helped alleviate chronic water scarcity across the State. Alongside water infrastructure, the Jyotigram Yojana and Krishi Mahotsav brought agricultural scientists directly to village doorsteps before the sowing season.

The grassroots principle of khet ka pani khet mein, gaon ka pani gaon mein (retaining field water in the field and village water in the village) captures a lasting truth: water security begins with local resource management.

Subsequent national programmes supporting micro-irrigation under PMKSY, direct income liquidity via PM-KISAN, and crop risk insurance have further expanded the scope of this agriculture across India. The priority now is ensuring that macro-level infrastructure consistently translates into better farm-gate decisions.

Beyond production: The farmer income imperative

Today, the central challenge facing Indian agriculture is no longer simply producing more; It is about ensuring that higher output generates remunerative and sustainable net returns.

Fragmented landholdings, rising cultivation costs, mandi price fluctuations and post-harvest loss continue to squeeze farm margins. Because sowing decisions often remain disconnected from market signals, bumper harvests frequently trigger farm-gate price crashes - even as India remains heavily dependent on imports for edible oils and pulses. Correcting this demand-supply mismatch requires placing market intelligence, crop diversification, warehousing and cold-chain infrastructure at the heart of agricultural planning.

Climate volatility adds another layer of urgency. Unseasonal downpours during harvest, terminal heat stress and shifting pest cycles mean that traditional calendar-based farming is no longer viable. Efficient irrigation, balanced soil nutrition, Integrated Pest Management (IPM) and real-time weather advisories are now operational necessities to protect farm profitability.

Science, trust and the last mile

Agricultural innovation delivers its full value only when it reaches farmers in an actionable and accessible form. In crop protection, our guiding principle is straightforward: spray right, not spray more. Accurate pest identification, choosing the right molecules, adhering to recommended doses and timely application are vital to cutting cultivation costs while protecting crops.

For the agri-input industry, responsibility extends far beyond supplying products. Building last-mile literacy through deeper partnerships with State agricultural universities, extension networks and Krishi Vigyan Kendras can turn laboratory research into daily field practice.

Equally critical is protecting the farmers from the menace of counterfeit and sub-standard agrochemicals, which destroy both crop yields and grower trust. Eliminating spurious inputs requires a coordinated push: stricter statutory enforcement, faster state laboratory testing of all the companies and not biased sample analysis of selected companies, farmer awareness drives and end-to-end digital authentication, which includes QR-code traceability – which is mandatory across the supply chain. Simultaneously, scaling precision technologies like agricultural drones that reduce water consumption by up to 80-90 per cent and minimise applicator exposure will accelerate field-level efficiency when backed by proper training.

Defining the next 25 years

India’s agricultural journey over the past quarter-century secured the nation’s food bowl security. The next 25 years must strengthen the economic prosperity of those who fill it with food.

Achieving that transition requires sustained alignment among policymakers, agricultural scientists, the input industry and cultivators focused on maximising sustainable net returns per acre while safeguarding every drop of water and every inch of topsoil. Ultimately, the agricultural transformation will be judged not just by how much India grows, but also by how reliably its farmers prosper.

The author is Chairman Emeritus, Dhanuka Agritech Ltd.

data.title: Maharashtra Targets Chemicals Hub Near Wadhavan Port As Policy Nears Final Stage
data.description:
The state is considering acquiring up to 5,000 acres near Wadhavan port for a dedicated chemicals park as India targets a USD 1 trillion sector by 2040

Maharashtra is in the final stage of formulating a dedicated chemicals sector policy and aims to announce it by the first week of November, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said on Thursday. The state is also exploring the acquisition of 2,500–5,000 acres near the upcoming Wadhavan port in Palghar district to develop a dedicated chemicals park.

Speaking at an industry event organised by the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), Fadnavis said the proposed policy would support the sector’s long-term growth. The state government has consulted industry leaders over the past few months to understand their requirements, with inputs expected to be incorporated into the policy.Among those consulted were Reliance Industries Executive Director Nikhil Meswani and UPL Chairman Jai Shroff. Fadnavis expressed confidence that the policy would encourage investors to expand their commitments to Maharashtra’s chemicals industry.

Chemicals Sector In Maharashtra

Fadnavis said the need for a dedicated chemicals policy became apparent after the state introduced its industrial policy last year. Maharashtra currently has 3,600 entities operating in the chemicals sector, which accounts for 19 per cent of the sector’s gross value added (GVA) and 17 per cent of chemical exports. The industry employs around 300,000 people in the state, he said.

He also highlighted Maharashtra’s existing port infrastructure, including Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA), which he described as the country’s largest container port, as a factor supporting the state’s role in the chemicals industry.

Proposed Chemicals Park Near Wadhavan

The state plans to develop a dedicated chemicals ecosystem near the greenfield Wadhavan port, which Fadnavis said is expected to be ready in about three years. The proposed land acquisition would support the establishment of a Bhavya Rasayanik Park, in line with the Union government’s announcement of Bhavya Rasayan Parks.

The proposed park is intended to create an industrial hub close to the port, supporting connectivity and the development of the chemicals sector.

India Targets USD 1 Trillion Chemicals Sector

Union Minister for Chemicals and Fertilisers J P Nadda, who also addressed the event, said the chemicals sector is currently valued at USD 220 billion, with a target of reaching USD 1 trillion by 2040.Nadda identified improved connectivity, supportive policies and industry leadership as factors that could contribute to the sector’s growth. He also said the government would facilitate environmental clearances for upcoming projects as part of its efforts to support capacity expansion.

The minister urged industry players to increase their focus on research and development (R&D). He added that advanced chemicals and petrochemicals are included in a newly launched Rs 1 lakh crore fund aimed at promoting research and innovation.

data.title: Cathie Wood-Led Ark Invest Sells PLTR, GOOG, SHOP Stocks — But Loads Up On PACB, FRNM And Other Biotech Firms
data.description:
Key points:
  • The trades spanned ARK's actively managed ETFs, with some positions appearing across more than one fund.
  • ARK Innovation ETF pared its stake in four prominent companies, namely, Palantir, Alphabet, Shopify, and Cloudflare.
  • The buying activity was concentrated in ARKG, where Ark added positions across a group of biotechnology companies rather than concentrating its purchases in a single stock.

Cathie Wood-led Ark Invest made a series of portfolio adjustments on Friday, trimming several technology and growth names while adding to a handful of biotechnology holdings.

The trades spanned ARK's actively managed ETFs, with some positions appearing across more than one fund. The activity included changes to both established holdings and smaller healthcare-focused names.

ARK Pares GOOG, PLTR, CRWD Stakes

Ark Invest reduced its exposure to several widely followed technology stocks during the session.

In the ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK), the firm sold 15,302 shares of Palantir Technologies Inc. (PLTR). It also sold 17,740 shares of Shopify Inc. (SHOP), 65,812 shares of Alphabet Inc. (GOOG) and 9,215 shares of Cloudflare Inc. (NET).

ARK had pared its stakes in Alphabet and Shopify last week as well. Alphabet and Cloudflare also appeared among the sales in the ARK Next Generation Technology ETF (ARKW). ARKW sold 11,355 shares of Alphabet and 2,786 shares of Cloudflare.

ARKW also sold 9,240 shares of Palantir, along with shares of CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. (CRWD), Circle Internet Group Inc. (CRCL), Roblox Corp. (RBLX), Rubrik Inc. (RBRK), Block Inc. (XYZ) and Everpure Inc. (P).

The ARKW trades included the sale of 42,499 shares of Circle and 34,222 shares of Roblox.

ARKG Continues To Load Up On Biotech Stocks

The buying activity was concentrated in the ARK Genomic Revolution ETF (ARKG), where Ark added positions across a group of biotechnology companies rather than concentrating its purchases in a single stock.

ARKG bought 68,266 shares of Pacific Biosciences of California Inc. (PACB), 22,479 shares of Scribe Therapeutics Inc. (SCTX) and 169,498 shares of Freenome Inc. (FRNM).

Pacific Biosciences was also added to the ARK Innovation ETF.

Across the two funds, Ark therefore bought Pacific Biosciences in both ARKG and ARKK, while the ARKG purchases also included Scribe Therapeutics and Freenome.

ARKG’s price closed up by nearly 1% in Friday’s regular trading session and rose nearly 0.2% during the after-hours trade. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around ARKG trended in the ‘neutral’ territory at the time of writing.

data.title: India's Scotch probe of Diageo, Pernod undermining India-UK pact benefits, trade group says
data.description:
Key points:
  • Indian investigators want firms to pay 150% duty on bulk Scotch, not 75%
  • Trade group says the pact’s tariff cut could become unavailable
  • Investigators searched Pernod, Diageo offices this month
  • Trade group seeks Indian commerce minister’s urgent intervention

By Aditya Kalra

India's move to exclude bulk Scotch imports from a reduced 75% tariff goes against provisions agreed in an India-UK trade deal, a group representing liquor makers Diageo and Pernod Ricard wrote in a letter seen by Reuters.

Whisky tariffs were a sticking point during the years of protracted negotiations leading up to the deal's July 15 implementation, though India ultimately agreed to halve import taxes on certain Scotch imports from 150% to 75% immediately and to 40% over 10 years.

The British government said "iconic UK products" like whiskies would benefit from the pact. Indian investigators, however, have privately told companies the reduced rate does not apply to bulk Scotch concentrates, creating the first significant dispute over the free trade agreement since it took effect.

India's Directorate of Revenue Intelligence searched the offices of Pernod and Diageo and questioned executives this month as part of an investigation into whether they misclassified imported products to benefit from the reduced rate.

CLASSIFICATION ISSUE RISKS UNDERMINING PACT, GROUP SAYS

In a letter to India's commerce minister on Friday, the International Spirits and Wines Association of India wrote that the classification issue "risks undermining, in practice, an important market-access benefit negotiated and agreed between India and the United Kingdom".

"The preferential tariff treatment negotiated ... could effectively become unavailable for these imports," continued the letter, a copy of which was seen by Reuters.

ISWAI declined to comment on its letter, while India's commerce ministry did not immediately respond.

Pernod, which counts India as its biggest market by volume, declined to comment. Diageo did not respond to a request for comment. Both told Reuters earlier this week that they were cooperating with Indian authorities carrying out the investigation.

In the British government's first comment on the controversy, a spokesperson said: "We are working with the government of India to resolve this issue to ensure UK businesses can export under the tariffs agreed in the trade deal."

Import tariff disputes have long been a sore point for foreign investors in India, who have in the past faced demands for large amounts of back tax. Such disputes have embroiled the likes of Samsung and Volkswagen.

Pernod faces antitrust cases in India and a $314 million back-tax demand from Indian authorities, who accuse it of undervaluing some imports. The company denies wrongdoing.

BIG IMPLICATIONS FOR INDIA'S DRINKS SECTOR

ISWAI's letter underscores the shockwaves the investigation has sent through India's $65 billion alcohol market. Britain accounts for almost 75% of India's imported spirits, primarily driven by Scotch whisky, according to Crisil Ratings.

Indian government inspectors have told companies that they do not benefit from the reduced 75% tariff on bulk imports of Scotch concentrates, which must be declared under a customs classification that attracts a 150% duty, three people with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters.

Pernod and Diageo import bulk concentrates, mixing them with other ingredients to produce hugely popular Indian brands like Royal Stag, Blenders Pride and McDowell’s.

The three people said companies including Diageo and Pernod believe concentrates imported from Britain should benefit from the new, lower tariff. ISWAI said in its letter that the India-UK agreement expressly provides preferential tariff treatment for whisky under the relevant tariff lines.

An urgent clarification could ensure market-access benefits negotiated by India and Britain are realised "while avoiding uncertainty and disruption for legitimate industry participants", the letter said.

On Saturday, the UK-based Scotch Whisky Association told Reuters in a statement that the import of bulk Scotch is key to whisky’s overall success in India and that upholding the core principles of the bilateral pact is vital.

The association, which counts Diageo and Pernod's Chivas Brothers as members, added the industry was "committed to working in partnership with the UK and Indian governments on the smooth implementation of the deal", so its benefits are unlocked.

data.title: Kalshi and Polymarket hit record $2.7 billion in weekly crypto volume
data.description:
Crypto-related prediction market volume on Kalshi and Polymarket reached a record $2.7 billion in a single week. Bitcoin price bets did most of the work.

That figure makes crypto the second most traded category on both platforms, behind only sports.

The record arrived in mid-October 2026. It reflects weekly notional volume, meaning the total face value of crypto-related event contracts traded across the two platforms.

The engine behind the surge is a new crop of high-frequency products. The standout is Kalshi's 15-minute up/down contract on Bitcoin.

Kalshi's Bitcoin contracts alone generated over $2 billion in a single week. That one subset accounts for the bulk of the combined $2.7 billion crypto total.

Polymarket is contributing too, mostly through its own shorter-duration crypto markets. Its US arm reported 15-minute Bitcoin volume of approximately $92 million to $101 million in its first full week of operation.

The crypto numbers sit inside a broader boom at Kalshi. The regulated US prediction market exchange set multiple weekly records during October.

Its peak came during the week of October 5 to 11, when total contract volume reached $19.03 billion. That figure covers every category on the platform, not just crypto.

Daily activity was similarly elevated. Kalshi's daily contract volume regularly landed between $3.9 billion and $4.4 billion during the month, with highs around $4.4 billion.

The growth in prediction markets comes as spot trading volumes across crypto decline. Coinbase and other platforms are expanding into prediction markets, looking for engagement that traditional buy-and-sell trading is no longer delivering at the same pace.

The most obvious takeaway is a shift in how people engage with Bitcoin. Record volume in short-duration event contracts points to strong appetite for fast, speculative exposure to price moves, rather than long-term ownership.

A 15-minute contract rewards speed and punishes hesitation. Traders using these products are effectively expressing a view on volatility in tiny increments.

For the platforms, the numbers validate the strategy, at least for now. Kalshi has demonstrated that crypto contracts can drive billions in weekly volume. Polymarket's US arm has shown it can attract meaningful early activity. Coinbase's move into the space suggests larger players see enough demand to justify the effort.

data.title: HP Nanda: A master of the old economy whose successors inherited a different world
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- Har Prasad Nanda wasn't quite the poor partition refugee that many other Indian entrepreneurs of the era were. Escorts Agents, his first venture, which he started in 1944 with his brother in Lahore, was a successful agency business of representing Westinghouse products. Unlike millions of others, he moved to India in 1947 with two cars and a fair bit of cash.

But the business was gone, along with the networks, and he had to start all over again in a newly independent country reeling from the burden of millions of displaced people who had to be fed, clothed, and resettled.

With capital, technology and manufacturing capacity in short supply, it wasn't a fertile environment for a young entrepreneur barely 30 years old. Yet, in such barren soil, Nanda planted the seeds of an engineering and automotive group that would eventually produce tractors, agricultural machinery, motorcycles and construction equipment.

The importance of each of these areas can't be stressed enough for India immediately after independence, as it struggled to lay its industrial base while modernizing its vast agricultural sector.

Nanda clearly had the ambition and the chops for the task. Legend has it that when he moved to Delhi, he chose to stay at the high-end Imperial Hotel rather than with relatives or at a cheaper place. This was not a man who was going to let the instability that came with displacement deflect him from his larger ambition.

Recognizing that food security would be one of the biggest challenges in India, he decided to place his bet on the demand for agricultural products rather than sticking to the easier agency business that he had in Lahore. Aptly, when the new company started off in 1948, it was named Escorts Agriculture Machines, marketing tractors and farm implements.

In 1949, the company became a franchise for the UK-based Massey Ferguson. The tie-up brought in much-needed technology and a prestigious international affiliation, both significant in a market where the competition included Eicher and TAFE. Over the years, others such as Mahindra and Punjab Tractors would also join the fray.

After initially importing tractors and selling them locally, Escorts started manufacturing them in 1961 with technology from Ursus of Poland. By the 1970s, boosted by a 1968 technical and financial collaboration with Ford, it had become one of the largest tractor makers in the country.

Soon, diversification into adjacent engineering markets, including its well-known Rajdoot motorcycles, followed. In an economy where first-time entrepreneurs were severely restricted by state controls, Nanda knew the importance of grabbing whatever opportunities were available.

Ironically, the very system he had to overcome to succeed would come to his aid when he faced his biggest jolt in business. Like many other industrialists of the era, Nanda controlled his company with a relatively small personal stake. This came back to haunt him in 1983 when the UK-based non-resident Indian businessman Swraj Paul picked up a 7.5% stake in Escorts and then threatened to take over the company.

Nanda needed the support of the government and the financial institutions to stave off that threat, which exposed the vulnerability of Indian promoters who controlled companies with tiny equity stakes. It also led to the tightening of rules governing takeovers.

Like many other business tycoons of the era, Nanda was a soft-spoken and informal person who rarely rushed people into anything. He and his wife, Raj, had two sons and two daughters.

He stepped down in 1994 following a heart bypass, dividing the business between his elder son Rajan, who took charge of Escorts and Anil, who was given the auto components business. The move came just three years after liberalization had opened up the economy, changing the rules of the business forever.

Nanda wisely decided that the altered environment needed fresh hands, and much like the Tata Group's sataraps had stepped aside for Ratan Tata, the time was right to bring in his own sons. The arrangement worked for a while, but eventually the brothers had a bitter falling out over the sale of Escorts Hospital.

By then, H.P. Nanda had passed away, leaving behind a group whose stagnant sales and slim profits ( Rs.9 crore profit on 1992-93 sales of Rs.982 crore) were a sign that decline had set in.

Nanda built Escorts into a powerhouse by reading the post-independence business environment better than most others. In his final years, though, the times just changed too rapidly even for him.

For more such stories, read The Enterprising Indian: Stories From India Inc.

data.title: Bank holiday today: Are SBI, HDFC, ICICI, PNB branches closed on 24 October for fourth Saturday? Check RBI calendar
data.description:
Bank holiday today, Oct. 24 -- Public and private lenders, including branches of the State Bank of India (SBI), HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Punjab National Bank (PNB), will be closed today, on 24 October for fourth Saturday off.

As per Reserve Bank of India (RBI) rules, all scheduled and non-scheduled banks observe mandatory closure on second and fourth Saturdays and every Sunday in a month. While in-branch services are shut, online services (net banking and app) remain operational.

Usually, in addition to the common national and gazetted holidays, or weekend offs, banks in India could have local holidays and festivals off, as required. The central bank releases its annual, official bank holiday list in January. Please contact your nearest local bank branch for their confirmed holiday schedule for 2026.

Banks, including the SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, PNB, Canara Bank, Bank of Baroda and other lenders across India will remain closed today, 24 October on account of it being the fourth Saturday of the month.

In RBI's holiday calendar, certain days are marked as non-working days for banks under "Negotiable Instruments Act" and other under "Banks' Closing of Accounts."

data.title: Five Indian stocks offering dividend yields up to 10%
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- A trailing dividend yield is calculated by dividing the dividends paid over the last 12 months by today's share price. While most screeners use this metric to rank high-yield dividend stocks, it can be misleading for three reasons: a one-time special dividend, changes in share count or business fundamentals after the payout, or a dividend that has already gone ex-dividend, meaning new buyers will not receive it. That is why examining these factors is crucial before investing in high-yield dividend stocks.

We have done the heavy lifting for you. Today, we look at five Indian stocks offering dividend yields of up to 10%.

We selected these five stocks by rebuilding each yield directly from its dividend record, using the share price on the dates shown. We also verified payout types (regular or special), record dates, earnings, and balance sheets.

Jagran Prakashan (JPL) is a highly diversified Indian media conglomerate. It operates 8 print publications across 13 states in 10 different languages. It's best known for publishing Dainik Jagran, the most widely read daily newspaper in India, with a readership of 69 million.

Through its subsidiary Music Broadcast, in which it holds a 74% stake, the company operates the popular Radio City brand. It boasts a 17% market share during FY26.

Jagran Prakashan paid a dividend of Rs.10 per share for FY26, including a special dividend of Rs.3. This implies a yield of 16%. Excluding the special dividend, the yield is 11.3%.

The company paid a total dividend of Rs.210 crore in FY26. JPL generated free cash flow of Rs.230 crore in FY26 and has consistently generated positive free cash flow for more than a decade. A strong net cash balance of over Rs.1,200 crore also helps the company fund dividends to shareholders.

In Q1FY27, its sales rose 8.5% to Rs.500 crore, but profit fell 9% to Rs.61 crore.

Looking ahead, JPL is navigating a mixed business environment. Dainik Jagran's advertisement revenue grew 4% year-on-year to Rs.870 crore in FY26, while circulation revenue declined 2% to Rs.280 crore.

JPL has implemented several initiatives to drive circulation growth. Management expects the results of these efforts to become apparent in the coming quarters.

SBI Funds Management is comfortably India's largest asset management company (AMC) by quarterly average assets under management (QAAUM), a position it has held since March 2021. Its mutual fund QAAUM stood at Rs.12.51 trillion as of 31 March 2026, or 15.3% of the industry. Its total QAAUM, including portfolio management, alternative investment fund and advisory mandates, reached Rs.29.46 trillion.

The company was listed on 21 July 2026 at Rs.613 a share, a 6.85% premium to the Rs.574 issue price, and currently trades at Rs.500.

Its numbers are temporarily elevated because of pre-IPO capital restructuring, including a special dividend and bonus issue, which reduced reported net worth.

Its high yield is a result of the interim dividend of Rs.70 a share paid in November 2025, before a bonus issue, and a Rs.9.60-a-share dividend in March 2026.

SBI Funds Management has a lower active equity share and leads passive funds, with a 27.9% share in index funds and ETFs, which earn much lower fees.

A meaningful part also comes from institutions and the Employee Provident Fund Organization (EPFO), another lower-yielding pool. Its equity performance has been middling, too, with less than 56% of equity AUM in the top two quartiles over three years.

Going forward, the company's prospects depend on the growth of passive investing in India, which continues to gain market share at the expense of active funds.

Expleo Solutions is not a pure-play cybersecurity firm. Cybersecurity is simply one growth area within its broader IT engineering, testing, BFSI technology, and digital transformation business. This opportunity is driven by rising enterprise spending on secure software, cloud solutions, automation, and regulatory compliance.

On 28 July 2026, Expleo Solutions' board recommended a final dividend of Rs.110 for FY26, which yields 12.25% at a share price of Rs.897.

The payout equals 138% of its FY26 EPS of Rs.79.89 and will cost roughly Rs.170 crore, compared with an FY26 net profit of about Rs.120 crore. As Expleo Group holds a 71.05% stake, most of this dividend flows to the promoters.

The company posted strong performance in Q1 FY27, with revenue growing 12.3% and operating margin expanding to 14.52% from 11.45%.

However, management signaled headwinds in a recent earnings call, warning that margin and top-line pressures will persist as part of a broader global trend. They also noted that overall deal ticket sizes are shrinking due to the rise of artificial intelligence.

To counter this, the company is shifting its FY27 strategy toward acquiring new clients, after prioritizing existing accounts last year. Meanwhile, it has inaugurated a significantly larger facility in Bengaluru to tap growing demand in aerospace and defence.

Following a multi-way demerger that spun off its aluminium, power, oil and gas, and iron and steel units into separately listed entities, the remaining listed Vedanta entity is now a focused base-metals company centered on zinc, copper, nickel, and ferrochrome.

Its domestic copper footprint comprises the Silvassa refinery and its two operational copper rod plants, along with the Thoothukudi smelter and refinery in Tamil Nadu. The Thoothukudi facility has been shut since 2018 following a pollution-related closure order, which the Supreme Court declined to overturn on review in November 2024.

Vedanta's current 13.79% yield reflects Rs.34 in FY26 dividends relative to a share price of Rs.246. Those dividends were paid on pre-demerger shares, which were priced near Rs.773 on 29 April 2026.

Overall, Vedanta maintains a track record of regular and generous dividend payouts.

Looking ahead, the company's growth prospects hinge on the ambitious copper expansion story tied to the Vedanta name: a roughly $270 crore plan to nearly quadruple annual output at Zambia's Konkola Copper Mines (KCM) to 270,000-300,000 tonnes by 2031. This initiative will be executed through a newly listed US entity, CopperTech Metals, situated one level up under Vedanta Resources-the UK-domiciled parent that has held KCM since 2004.

Its roadmap also relies on Hindustan Zinc's growth vision, driven by smelter expansions across existing locations. While these expansions are unlikely to materialize in FY27, strong execution momentum could bode well for the stock. Dividend distributions from Hindustan Zinc remain equally crucial, given Vedanta's majority stake in the company.

Established in 1980, Indo Borax manufactures boron-based chemicals such as boric acid, borax, DOT, lithium hydroxide monohydrate, and related derivatives.

Its offerings serve sectors spanning steel, refractories, glass, ceramics, pharmaceuticals, personal care, and agriculture, with boric acid serving as a key component in steel industry ramming mass and furnace linings.

The company's core manufacturing hub at Pithampur, Madhya Pradesh, has a rated capacity of 20,000 MT for boric acid and 6,000 MT for DOT.

For FY26, Indo Borax distributed Rs.40 per share to shareholders-consisting of a Rs.10 final dividend and a Rs.30 special payout-against a record date of 21 July 2026.

The Rs.130 crore dividend payout represented 2.6 times the company's FY26 profit and roughly 61% of its Rs.210 crore investment portfolio as of March 2026.

Ownership has also shifted recently: a consortium led by Zenrock Chemicals acquired a 50.80% stake in the company under an agreement signed on 15 December 2025. Subsequently, on 20 August 2026, Indo Borax agreed to acquire 64.26% of Kronox Lab Sciences for Rs.250 crore. It also launched an open offer to acquire up to an additional 25.79% of Kronox at Rs.157.27 per share, representing an outlay of up to Rs.1,510 crore in cash.

Looking ahead, Indo Borax plans a capital expenditure of around Rs.90 crore ( Rs.900 million) across FY27 and FY28, funded entirely through internal accruals. Of this total, approximately Rs.20 crore ( Rs.200 million) is earmarked for setting up 4,000 MT of boron oxide capacity, with the remaining Rs.70 crore ( Rs.700 million) dedicated to adding 10,000 MT of boric acid capacity.

Commercial operations at the new facilities are expected to begin in FY29. Consequently, meaningful growth beyond current debottlenecking efforts will hinge on the timely execution and ramp-up of these proposed capacities, alongside market development for boric acid and its downstream products.

Investing in high-yield dividend stocks might seem like a no-brainer, but it comes with several critical caveats.

First, dividend yield is a backward-looking metric. Special dividends are rarely repeated. Second, major corporate actions-such as bonuses or demergers, as seen with SBI Funds and Vedanta-alter the overall share count after a dividend has been paid out. Finally, a payout ratio exceeding 100% of earnings is funded out of reserves and savings, making it unsustainable over the long run.

As always, investors should thoroughly evaluate business quality, financial strength, management execution, corporate governance, and valuation before drawing any investment conclusions.

Happy investing!

Key points:
  • Trump's Iran war, tariffs turn foreign policy into kitchen-table issue
  • Voter discontent threatens Republican control of Congress, complicating Trump agenda
  • Question is whether shift in power balance constrains or unfetters Trump on world stage

By Matt Spetalnick

Foreign policy is rarely the deciding factor in US midterm elections, when economic considerations usually drive voters’ choices.

But this time, with Donald Trump’s war against Iran and his sweeping tariff campaign pushing up costs for Americans, a president’s approach to world affairs has itself become a pocketbook issue.

As the November 3 elections approach, there are growing signs that voters are drawing that connection directly, creating a major liability for Trump and his fellow Republicans and imperiling their control of Congress.

Those include a Reuters/Ipsos poll earlier this month showing some 78% of Americans blame Trump's policies for rising prices that are outpacing their earnings.

Not since 2006, when President George W. Bush’s Republicans lost both legislative chambers while he was mired in the unpopular Iraq war, has a US leader’s handling of international events appeared so central to shaping the midterms outcome.

The political backlash for Trump could be even bigger, with opinion polls showing that voters feel the economic pain from high gas prices and rising grocery bills in a way that they didn’t two decades ago.

“The bottom line is people are experiencing the impact of Trump’s war and other policies,” said Christopher Preble, a senior fellow at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington. “Now voters have a chance to register their discontent with how he’s dealing with all this.”

POLITICS DRIVING FOREIGN POLICY

With Trump’s approval ratings touching historic lows, he has left little doubt, despite his public claims to the contrary, that he sees the straight line voters are drawing between his foreign policy and their cost of living.

That has prompted some controversial policy moves in the run-up to the elections.

Chief among them was Trump’s lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel exports aimed at bringing down fuel prices, a step his critics, including some fellow Republicans, say reinforces the impression that he is increasingly siding with Moscow in its war in Ukraine.

He has also pressed Kyiv to halt strikes on Russian refineries as he tries to shift the blame for high US gasoline prices despite experts saying the surge in energy costs is mainly the result of the war he launched alongside Israel against Iran nearly eight months ago.

At the same time, he has promised not to order any new attack on Iran before the midterms, though the US and Israel are widely reported to be preparing for a possible major escalation after the elections.

Polls have shown that most voters oppose the war initiated by Trump, who had campaigned on avoiding new foreign interventions. He has insisted Americans should accept temporarily higher gas prices so that he can block Iran from developing a nuclear weapon.

Iran says its nuclear program is for civilian purposes. The UN nuclear watchdog and US intelligence community have assessed that Tehran shuttered a nuclear weapons development program in 2003.

Some Republican candidates have distanced themselves from Trump on matters ranging from the conflict in the Middle East to the trade war with Canada and his pressure campaign against Ukraine.

For its part, Iran has sought to keep oil prices high and hurt Trump in the midterms by deploying new tactics to target ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz and deliberately prolonging the diplomatic stalemate, senior Iranian officials have told Reuters.

Defending the administration's approach, White House spokesman Matt Middleton said: "President Trump has always been clear about temporary market disruptions as a result of the conflict in Iran, but the contrast between President Trump’s economic record and Democrats’ ruinous alternative is clear."

‘IT’S THE ECONOMY, STUPID’

Midterm elections historically have been seen as a referendum on the performance of the incumbent in the White House.

And in one election after another in recent decades, the conventional wisdom has been that economic concerns - “it’s the economy, stupid,” as the Clinton-era adage goes - dominate voters’ choices.

Opinion polls for this year’s midterms, including the Reuters/Ipsos survey, show that while voters rank foreign policy low on their list of priorities, it is clear that most Americans see some of Trump’s signature moves on the world stage, such as the Iran war and tariffs, feeding into their higher costs.

Other polls have shown that a majority of Americans have also soured more broadly on Trump’s international approach.

The Chicago Council on Global Affairs said its latest nationwide survey “finds that most Americans believe the Trump administration’s foreign policy actions have negatively impacted America’s global standing and hurt national and household economic conditions.”

Since returning to the White House last year, Trump has shaken up the rules-based global order that Washington helped create from the ashes of World War Two while his relations with allies have steadily worsened and the limits of US power have been increasingly exposed, analysts say.

LEGISLATIVE BALANCE OF POWER IN PLAY

Against this backdrop, Democrats are widely projected to gain control of the House of Representatives in the midterms, with the Senate also seen as increasingly in play.

For Republicans, losing either chamber could complicate Trump's agenda in the last two years of his second term.

But even with a shift in the balance of power on Capitol Hill on November 3, lawmakers will have a hard time reining in Trump’s capacity to pursue foreign policy as he sees fit.

Once the ballots are counted, a big question will be whether Trump will feel either restricted or emboldened on the world stage as he enters what is traditionally considered a lame-duck phase - when a president is barred from running again and no longer faces electoral consequences for decisions made.

“For many presidents who feel politically constrained (at home), foreign policy is the area where they are able to act with relative freedom,” said Jon Alterman of the Center for Strategic and International Studies think tank in Washington.

Analysts say Trump's handling of adversaries such as Iran, Russia, China and even Cuba or his approach to allies across the globe could go either way — or he could simply lose interest and double down on his string of construction projects, such as the White House ballroom.

data.title: Estée Lauder Is Getting A Makeover and Faces A Beautiful Future — Barrons.com
AI and EV Boom Draws $690 Million in Advanced Materials Investment Plans to Thailand
data.description:
EQS Newswire / 24/10/2026 / 06:30 CET/CEST

BANGKOK, THAILAND - Media OutReach Newswire - 24 October 2026 - Makers of the capacitors, magnets and battery materials inside AI servers and electric vehicles (EVs) are lining up to invest in Thailand. Since 2023, they have filed 35 advanced materials projects worth about $690 million (23.5 billion baht) with the Thailand Board of Investment (BOI), the government's investment promotion agency. Surging demand for AI, EVs, and clean energy is pushing global suppliers to build upstream capacity in the country.

Mr. Narit Therdsteerasukdi, Secretary General of the Thailand Board of Investment (BOI)

The projects, filed through the first half of 2026, cover multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs), thermal graphite films, high-performance ceramics, battery and fuel-cell materials, neodymium magnets, glass and quartz fabrics for printed circuit boards, and nanomaterials for precision manufacturing. Together they mark a shift for one of Southeast Asia's largest economies from downstream assembly toward the high-value materials on which future industries are built. In AI computing and clean energy, lighter, more heat-resistant and more conductive materials determine how well devices perform. MLCCs are essential components in products from smartphones to AI servers, and a single high-end server can use up to 30,000 of them. "The world is moving toward products that are smaller and lighter, yet stronger and more efficient," said Mr. Narit Therdsteerasukdi, Secretary General of the Thailand Board of Investment. "Producing advanced materials in Thailand is key to building sustainable industrial capacity, reducing reliance on imports, and opening the door for Thai companies to join higher-value supply chains." Thailand is already a production base for leading component makers, including Japan's Murata Electronics, which holds more than 35 percent of the global MLCC market, and Kyocera AVX Components, the world's top tantalum capacitor maker. Among the new projects, Taiwan's Fultech Fiber Glass makes glass fabric for printed circuit boards, including high-performance grades for AI servers. Jones Tech produces synthetic and natural graphite films that carry heat away from electronic devices. Beyond electronics, the projects strengthen supply chains for electric vehicles, batteries, and clean energy, from BGN Thai's coated foils for lithium-ion batteries and Phinis Well's neodymium magnets for EV motors to Xinyuan Graphite's bipolar plates for hydrogen fuel cells. CoorsTek Advanced Materials, a subsidiary of US-based CoorsTek — a global leader in engineered ceramics for the semiconductor and aerospace industries — has invested in producing ceramics for automotive pressure sensors and silicon nitride balls for hybrid bearings in EVs and wind turbines. Golden Egret Cemented Carbide is making tungsten carbide powders for precision cutting tools, reinforcing Thailand's base for high-precision manufacturing. "The advanced materials industry taking root in Thailand today is the foundation of tomorrow's supply chains in electronics, EVs, batteries, and clean energy," Mr. Narit said. "The BOI will keep building this investment base, strengthening upstream materials and components, and supporting R&D, technology, and workforce development, to move Thailand from downstream to upstream production and make it the region's advanced materials hub." Note: USD conversions are based on the Bank of Thailand's average selling rate of approximately 33.76 baht per USD. Thailand Board of Investment (BOI)

Established in 1966, the Thailand Board of Investment (BOI) has spent six decades promoting high-value investment from both foreign and Thai investors, strengthening the country's competitiveness and driving its transition toward a sustainable, balanced new economy. data.title: KEC International wins ₹2,872 crore orders from Power Grid, its largest India T&D order
data.description:
KEC International has secured orders worth ₹2,872 crore from Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd (PGCIL) for the design, supply and installation of 765 kV transmission lines, according to a company release filed with the BSE on October 24.

The company said the orders mark the largest-ever single order for its India transmission and distribution (T&D) business. The projects are linked to the evacuation of 8.5 gigawatts (GW) of renewable energy from Gujarat.

The orders have significantly expanded KEC International's domestic T&D order book, the company said in the release.

Vimal Kejriwal, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of KEC International, said the company had secured the orders amid strong momentum in its T&D business.

"These prestigious 765 kV projects, associated with the evacuation of 8.5 GW of renewable energy from Gujarat, have substantially expanded our India T&D order book," Kejriwal said.

The company remained confident about the growth prospects of India's T&D market, supported by rising energy demand and the country's continued focus on strengthening transmission infrastructure.

With the latest order wins, KEC International's year-to-date order intake has crossed ₹13,500 crore, including around ₹9,500 crore from its T&D business, the release stated.

Mumbai-based KEC International is the flagship company of RPG Group and operates in infrastructure engineering, procurement and construction. Its businesses include power transmission and distribution, civil construction, transportation, renewable energy, oil and gas pipelines, and cables and conductors.

KEC shares closed around 1.5% down at ₹327 apiece on the NSE on Friday, October 23. The stock has shed nearly 56% so far this year.

data.title: Bolsonaro and Lula clash on living costs, corruption in final Brazil election debate
data.description:
Key points:
  • Polls show Bolsonaro and Lula close ahead of Sunday runoff
  • Bolsonaro criticized food prices, Lula defended wage policy

By Andre Romani

Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva sparred over the cost of living and traded personal attacks on Friday in the last presidential debate before Sunday's runoff, as both candidates sought to win over undecided voters amid a tight race.

Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, led Lula in the first round of the election earlier this month, but opinion polls have shown the two candidates about even this week after the gap between them narrowed.

Bolsonaro and Lula repeated their campaign proposals during the over two-hour debate hosted by Globo, Brazil's most-watched TV channel, focusing on themes such as the cost of living, welfare and security, while exchanging allegations of corruption.

Lula, who is seeking his fourth term after winning back the presidency in 2022, has defended his government's above-inflation minimum wage increases and stressed that his administration helped millions of Brazilians to escape hunger.

The president said the younger Bolsonaro "is like students studying for college entrance exams. They can memorize things, but they can't learn." He also said that "in the gated community where Bolsonaro lives, people don't go hungry."

Bolsonaro responded by saying food prices for Brazilians rose during Lula's administration, and he criticized a tax reform approved by the current government, projecting the new rules would raise the tax burden on consumers.

"Lula doesn't even remember the last time he went grocery shopping because he lives in a luxury palace now."

The two candidates mostly limited the discussion to pre-established themes in the first few segments of the debate, toning down the personal attacks that marked the only previous debate in the campaign between the two.

At one point, Bolsonaro apologized to Lula after saying the president gives to Brazilians with one hand but "takes away with nine fingers." Lula lost his left little finger in an accident while working as a lathe operator in a factory.

"I will not accept some rich guy, with a highly questionable political practice, calling me 'nine fingers,'" the incumbent said, demanding a retraction.

"Lula, if I offended you by calling you 'nine fingers,' then I sincerely apologize, I sincerely apologize," Bolsonaro said. But he added: "Will you apologize to Brazilians suffering from insecurity ... in debt?"

The discussion heated up in the last minutes of the debate, when both candidates were allowed to interact without moderation, as Lula and Bolsonaro sought to link each other to the fraud involving lender Banco Master.

Lula pressed Bolsonaro on alleged links to the bank's jailed banker Daniel Vorcaro, and Bolsonaro questioned Lula about accusations involving his son and a pension fraud.

The debate was one of the campaign's final events, as Brazilian electoral law bars the candidates from broadcasting radio and TV campaign advertising starting on Saturday. They can still hold rallies until the final hours of the day.

data.title: DGCA Extends Pilot Rest Rule Deadline to March
data.description:
As Airline Face cost pressures... Arindam Majumder New Delhi: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) extended the deadline for the full implementation of revised pilot rest rules by five months to March 31, 2027, as airlines grapple with rising operating costs and concerns over the impact of the guidelines on crew availability, people aware of the matter said.

The latest extension granted earlier this week was the third. The previous relaxation followed IndiGo's operational crisis last December, when India's largest airline cancelled thousands of flights amid a crew shortage. The revised Flight Duty Time Limitations rules, notified early last year, revised the definition of night duty to extend the period covered by an hour, from midnight to 6 am instead of midnight to 5 am.

They also capped the number of landings a pilot can undertake during this period at two and limited duty to 10 hours. In December, the DGCA allowed airlines to operate with three landings when a pilot's duty fell between midnight and 1:55 am or between 5 am and 6 am. Airlines were required to provide rest equivalent to twice the duty period for such operations.

The relaxations, due to expire on October 31, will now continue until March 31. Associations of pilots have opposed such repeated extensions, arguing that they undermine the objective of the revised safety regulations. "Airlines had raised concerns about implementing these rules when the cost structure is already high due to high fuel costs.

They have slowed down hiring of pilots. As a regulator, the DGCA has to take into consideration safety and viable operations," a government official said, adding that no further exemptions would be granted after March 31. The Federation of Indian Airlines, whose members include IndiGo, Air India and SpiceJet, said that the revised rules could increase their pilot requirements by 25%. Airlines also cited high aviation turbine fuel prices, airspace restrictions, additional crew expenses and rupee depreciation as pressures on their finances.

The Federation of Indian Pilots, meanwhile, urged the government to withdraw the relaxations, saying that the regulator was normalising exceptional arrangements rather than forcing airlines to comply with laws. "The five-month extension risked prolonging arrangements intended to address temporary operational difficulties, and gives an impression that mandatory safety requirements may be deferred whenever operational pressures arise," it said in a letter to civil aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu that ET has seen.

data.title: Airlines Oppose Any Cuts in Slots at Mumbai Airport
data.description:
Forum Gandhi Mumbai: Airlines operating at the Adani Group-controlled Mumbai airport opposed any unilateral reduction or cancellation of flight slots under a proposed traffic reallocation plan for summer 2027, according to letters seen by ET. They asked the airport operator to provide capacity data and details of Terminal 1's redevelopment plan before proceeding with the proposal.

The dispute centres on how the airport will accommodate airlines during the redevelopment of Terminal 1, and whether flight slots will need to be reduced or traffic shifted to manage capacity. At a meeting scheduled for October 28, airlines want Mumbai International Airport Ltd (MIAL), which operates the airport, to provide the actual capacity of the two terminals of the airport, details of the refurbishment timeline and an update on the planned capacity addition at Terminal 2, before decisions are made on the Summer 2027 transition plan.

In a letter on Friday, the Airport Operators Committee (AOC) in Mumbai reiterated that MIAL must comply with the Ministry of Civil Aviation's May 2013 slot-allocation guidelines and the International Air Transport Association's Worldwide Airport Slot Guidelines. Traffic reallocation must not be implemented unilaterally without compliance with the applicable procedures, it said.

The AOC said no substantiated justification was provided for reducing or cancelling slots at the airport, claiming that Terminal 1 was currently handling less than 10 million passengers per annum (MPPA) and that there was an expected capacity addition of 5 MPPA at Terminal 2 by next March. "Any such proposal must be supported by verifiable capacity assessments, operational data and a clear, evidence-based justification," the committee said.

Terminal 1's current capacity is 15 million passengers and the airport operator plans to increase it to 20 million. MIAL earlier this week told airlines that they were free to shift some or all of their operations to the new airport in Navi Mumbai, suspend services until its Terminal 1 reopens in 2030, or pursue other options from summer 2027. The Navi Mumbai airport is also controlled by Adani Airports Holdings.

Meanwhile, the MIAL chief airport officer's office on Friday sent a second reminder to airlines that had not yet held discussions with the airport operator on the transition plan. It asked them to arrange consultations with the airport's network-planning and commercial teams to help finalise the plan ahead of the October 28 stakeholder meeting. In its response, the AOC said airlines supported the T1 refurbishment "as a priority and without any further delay".

data.title: IndusInd Returns to Black in Q2 as Provisions Halve
data.description:
Our Bureau Mumbai: IndusInd Bank reported a consolidated net profit of 1,242 crore at the end of the September quarter against a net loss of 437 crore a year earlier, helped by a sharp decline in provisions, higher fee income and an improvement in asset quality.

The private sector lender's net interest income (NII) rose 4% year-on-year to 4,569 crore at the end of the September quarter from 4,409 crore in the same quarter last year, while other income jumped 36% to 2,248 crore from 1,651 crore. The improvement in profitability was largely driven by a 54% year-on-year decline in provisions and contingencies to 1,223 crore from 2,631 crore, reflecting moderation in credit stress.

Gross slippages, or fresh additions to bad loans, declined 42% during the September quarter to 1,460 crore from 2,537 crore a year earlier. "(The quarter) reflects the growing strength of the franchise and the progress we have made in rebuilding momentum across the bank," Rajiv Anand, MD, IndusInd Bank, said after the earnings. "Growth has strengthened, profitability has improved, asset quality trends remain encouraging, and our funding profile is becoming more granular and resilient." Asset quality improved, with the gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio declining 87 basis points to 2.7% from 3.6% a year earlier. The net NPA ratio fell 21 basis points to 0.8% from 1.0%. Despite the improvement in earnings, net interest margins remained under pressure. NIM narrowed by 9 basis points year-on-year to 3.2% from 3.3%, with the bank attributing the pressure to mobilisation of foreign currency non-resident (FCNR-B) deposits. One basis point is a hundredth of a percentage point.

The bank's loan book expanded 11% year-on-year to 3.6 lakh crore from 3.3 lakh crore. Retail advances rose 13% to 2.1 lakh crore, while wholesale advances increased 10% to 1.5 lakh crore. Within retail lending, consumer banking advances surged 38% to 76,341 crore, although the growth included 16,564 crore of advances linked to FCNR(B) deposits.

Vehicle finance loans grew 5% to 1.0 lakh crore, while rural banking advances contracted 6% to 33,338 crore. The microloan portfolio shrank 18% year-on-year to 17,571 crore from 21,321 crore, reflecting continued contraction in the segment. Credit card receivables declined 15% to 9,167 crore from 10,747 crore. Home loans, however, rose 39% to 7,733 crore. On the liabilities side, deposits grew 10% year-on-year to 4.3 lakh crore from 3.9 lakh crore. Current account deposits increased 15% to 36,742 crore, while savings account deposits declined 5% to 83,024 crore.

data.title: Shriram Fin Q2 Net up 59%
data.description:
Our Bureau Mumbai: Shriram Finance, in which Japan's Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG) has a significant stake, reported a 59.4% year-on-year rise in standalone net profit to 3,677 crore for the quarter ended September 2026, driven by growth in net interest income and lower finance costs.

It reported a net profit of 2,307 crore a year earlier. Net interest margin (NIM), a measure of core profitability, improved to 9.52% from 8.19% a year earlier. "Our long-term guidance has consistently been around 8.5%, but it will take some time to return to that level. For the next two quarters, we expect NIM to remain around 9%," said Parag Sharma, MD & CEO, in an interview with ET. He attributed growth in profit to two factors. "The first was growth in business volumes, and the second was the substantial benefit from lower interest costs, which lifted net interest income," he added.

Net interest income rose 38% to 8,661 crore from 6,267 crore. The increase was driven by a 15.6% rise in interest income to 13,669 crore, while interest expenses fell 9.9% to 5,008 crore. Operating profit increased 53.3% to 6,809 crore, while the cost-to-income ratio improved to 22.52% from 27.76%. Core operating profit, which excludes other income, rose 53.5% to 6,682 crore.

The profit growth came despite a 41% increase in loan losses and provisions to 1,877 crore from 1,333 crore in the year-ago quarter. On a sequential basis, provisions rose 28.3%. Total income increased 15.8% to 13,799 crore, while profit before tax rose 58.6% to 4,932 crore. Net profit was 6.8% higher sequentially than 3,445 crore in the June quarter. Assets under management (AUM) grew 17% year on year and 4.9% sequentially to 3.29 lakh crore at the end of September. The broader vehicle and equipment portfolio stood at 2.61 lakh crore, accounting for 79.46% of total AUM.

data.title: SBI Cards Q2 Profit Jumps 75%
data.description:
Our Bureau Mumbai: SBI Cards and Payment Services reported a 75% year-on-year rise in net profit to 778 crore for the September quarter, driven by a sharp decline in credit costs and an improvement in asset quality, even as corporate card spends contracted and outstanding receivables declined.

The company had reported a net profit of 445 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Total income increased 3% year on year to 5,302 crore from 5,136 crore. Impairment losses and bad debt expenses declined 37% year on year to 819 crore from 1,293 crore, providing a significant boost to profitability.

The company's net interest margin (NIM) narrowed by 42 basis points year on year to 10.8%. "During Q2 of FY27, we continued to focus on building a healthy, sustainable and well-balanced portfolio, while maintaining our priorities around profitable customer acquisition, customer engagement, operating efficiency and portfolio quality," said Salila Pande, MD, SBI Cards, during the post-earnings analyst call.

The company's gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio improved to 1.90% at September-end from 2.85% a year earlier, while the net NPA ratio declined to 0.77% from 1.29%. Gross write-offs fell 34% year on year to 849 crore, reflecting improved credit quality in its portfolio. However, growth in the underlying business remained modest. Overall credit card spends increased just 3% year on year to 1.11 lakh crore from 1.07 lakh crore.

data.title: Pawan Hans Asked to Chart Five-Year Turnaround Plan by This Year End
data.description:
Anuradha Shukla New Delhi: The Department of Public Enterprises (DPE) has asked state-owned helicopter operator Pawan Hans to submit a five-year turnaround plan by December, focusing on financial and organisational restructuring, steps to enhance operational and fleet efficiencies, and the identification of new verticals and revenue streams.

The move comes amid the government's push to handhold central public sector enterprises (CPSEs) with strategic potential and improve their performance. The communication, sent in the first week of October, follows a September meeting between the Pawan Hans management and senior DPE officials.

Pawan Hans management is also planning to engage a senior consultant to help prepare the plan, officials said. "There is a lot of potential for the state-owned helicopter operator and, with proper hand-holding, it can grow multifold," a senior official said. The move follows an instruction by a committee headed by cabinet secretary TV Somanathan, which has recommended handholding CPSEs that can be strategic to the medium- to long-term growth of the country.

The roadmap is expected to assess opportunities in heli-tourism, religious tourism, helicopter emergency medical services, regional connectivity and other aviation-related businesses. The development of heliports and services for remote and underserved destinations could feature in the expansion strategy. Pawan Hans has separately been exploring electric seaplane technology. In August, it signed a non-binding MoU with Norway's Noemi Aerospace to explore collaboration in electric seaplanes and sustainable aviation.

The turnaround exercise follows the collapse of an earlier divestment attempt. In May 2022, the government selected a consortium led by Star9 Mobility Pvt Ltd to acquire 51% stake in the company for 211.14 crore. The process was subsequently called off in July 2023 amid pending legal cases. The civil aviation ministry is the administrative ministry for Pawan Hans, while the DPE, under the finance ministry, frames policy guidelines relating to the performance and management of CPSEs.

The ministry has already allocated 450 crore for fleet modernisation, linking the company's expansion plans to the government's push to strengthen indigenous helicopter capacity and improve connectivity to remote regions under the Udaan scheme. The proposed induction of Dhruv helicopters from Hindustan Aeronautics into Pawan Hans is also part of the Centre's effort to strengthen indigenous aviation capabilities.

data.title: Coforge Q2 Net Profit Jumps 56.5% to 588 cr on Encora Deal
data.description:
Our Bureau Bengaluru: Mid-size IT services firm Coforge reported a 56.5% year-on-year increase in net profit to 588.1 crore for the second quarter of the fiscal year 2027, aided by a full-quarter contribution from its acquisition of engineering services firm Encora for $2.35 billion.

Sequentially, net profit rose 13.4%. Revenue for the September quarter increased 53.6% year-on-year and 11.6% sequentially to 6,170.8 crore. In dollar terms, revenue stood at $652.2 million, up 10.1% from the preceding quarter on constant currency terms. Contribution from the Encora acquisition was a major reason for the revenue growth this quarter along with large deals. "The demand slowdown that we are talking about is largely on account of the fact that the procurement-driven RFPs have slowed down.

The intensity of the ask around delivering AI-led transformation for enterprises is only getting stronger," chief executive officer Sudhir Singh said in the post-earnings analyst call. and close deals without getting into fistcuffs with other providers around pricing," he added. The second quarter was the first to fully consolidate Encora, since its acquisition in December 2025.

Singh said its margin expansion was ahead of plan and revenue growth should mirror Coforge's from Q3, with the largest deal in Coforge's pipeline involving an Encora client. Encora contributed about $147-$148 million in revenue on a constant-currency basis during the quarter, broadly flat against the preceding quarter's comparable full-quarter revenue, chief financial officer Saurabh Goyal said. Deal wins by total contract value stood at $1.04 billion, compared with $691 million in the preceding quarter and $514 million a year earlier.
